items.name: apple-design
items.author: emilkowalski
items.description: A frontend developer building gesture-driven UI, springs, or sheet interactions applies Apple's fluid-interface principles translated to CSS, Pointer Events, and Motion.
items.summary: apple-design translates Apple's approach to fluid, physical interface motion - chiefly from the WWDC 2018 Designing Fluid Interfaces talk - into web implementation guidance using CSS, Pointer Events, requestAnimationFrame, and spring libraries like Motion. Its core rules: respond on pointer-down rather than release, track drags 1:1 while respecting the grab offset, keep a velocity history for release momentum, and make every animation interruptible by animating from the current presentation value. Use it when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, spring animations, translucent materials, typography details, or reduced-motion support.

items.name: improve-animations

items.summary: improve-animations surveys a codebase's animation and motion code as a senior motion advisor, then produces a prioritized audit and self-contained implementation plans for other agents to execute. It is strictly read-only on source: recon maps the motion stack, tokens, and how often each animated element is hit; a parallel audit judges against eight categories (purpose, easing and duration, physicality, interruptibility, performance, and more) using Emil Kowalski's rule catalog; vetted findings become plans precise enough — exact easings, durations, file paths — for a zero-context executor. Use it for a motion roadmap rather than a single-diff review.

items.name: hyperframes-audio

items.name: find-animation-opportunities
items.author: emilkowalski
items.description: Design engineers sweep a codebase or UI for moments that would genuinely benefit from motion and get precise animation recipes, with most candidates deliberately rejected.
items.summary: A restraint-first search skill from Emil Kowalski's animation suite that sweeps an interface for places that should animate but do not, and rejects everything else. Every candidate must pass a four-part gate: usage frequency (keyboard-driven and 100+/day actions are auto-rejected), a named purpose (feedback, spatial consistency, state indication, preventing jarring changes, explanation, or rare-tier delight), a duration budget under 300ms for UI, and interruption behavior. It is read-only and caps output at 5-7 suggestions with exact values, handing implementation to improve-animations or another agent.

It also catches common mismatches like hand-built toasts or div-based primitives.

items.name: azure-app-onboard

Guardrails include a healing loop that asks the user after repeated failures and a region lock requiring re-approval if the deployment location drifts from the plan. It is an orchestrated sub-skill, not directly user-routable.

items.name: azure-app-onboard-prereq

It never runs package installs or test suites; downstream onboard phases consume prereq-output.json artifacts.

items.name: prototype
items.author: emilkowalski
items.description: Design engineers use it to build several genuinely different working versions of one UI piece behind a visual picker, flip through them live, and promote the winner into the codebase.
items.summary: Prototype is a divergence skill for UI design exploration: given one described piece of UI (a toast, a pricing card, a hold-to-delete button), it builds several genuinely different fully-working versions and renders them behind a visual picker so the user can flip through them live and promote a winner. Variants must each diverge on a named axis - layout, density, personality, motion, or interaction model - while individually meeting Emil Kowalski's motion standards (ease-out entrances, sub-300ms durations, transform/opacity only, reduced-motion handled) and using the project's own tokens. Exploration happens in an isolated prototype surface; only the chosen variant is integrated, and the surface is deleted afterward. Explicit invocation only.

items.name: remotion-render
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Developers producing programmatic videos with Remotion use it for the correct render commands, including stills and transparent video output.
items.summary: A short official Remotion skill covering video rendering best practices: use npx remotion render for videos and npx remotion still for still frames, with pointers to the full CLI option docs and a companion reference for rendering videos with transparency. Reach for it when a Remotion project needs its compositions rendered to output files.

items.name: remotion-create
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: A developer scaffolds a new Remotion project and composition to produce a programmatic video in React, from create-video setup through Studio preview.
items.summary: remotion-create walks through starting a new Remotion video project: scaffolding with npx create-video@latest, adding React markup for the composition, and launching the Studio preview server. It delegates design guidance to companion skills in the same repository - Remotion markup best practices, video layout rules, and interactivity best practices that keep compositions editable in Remotion Studio's visual mode - and includes a reference for using TailwindCSS. Reach for it when the task is specifically to create a new Remotion project or composition; follow-up editing work routes to the remotion-best-practices skill.

items.name: remotion-captions
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Remotion users generate, display, and import captions in programmatic videos using the typed Caption JSON format.
items.summary: remotion-captions defines how to handle captions in Remotion videos: all captions are processed as JSON using the Caption type from @remotion/captions, with per-cue text and millisecond timing. It links out to focused instructions for three tasks — transcribing video and audio files to generate captions, displaying captions in a composition, and importing existing .srt subtitle files. Use it whenever a Remotion project needs subtitles or captions.

items.name: remotion-markup
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Developers writing Remotion React markup follow its rules (useCurrentFrame + interpolate, Sequence timing, staticFile assets) so compositions render video correctly.
items.summary: Official best practices for writing Remotion React markup, the JSX that renders programmatic video. It mandates frame-based animation with useCurrentFrame() and interpolate() (inline in the style prop, with Easing.bezier for custom timing), forbids CSS transitions and Tailwind animation classes because they do not render correctly, and covers Interactive elements for Studio editing, staticFile() asset references, @remotion/media for audio and video, and Sequence for delaying and bounding content. Pointers cover maps and text-highlight annotations. Load the companion remotion-best-practices skill when markup is not the concern.

items.name: remotion-interactivity
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: A Remotion developer structures animation code so compositions stay editable in Remotion Studio Visual Mode and video clips are editable in the timeline.
items.summary: remotion-interactivity is a pointer skill with best practices for writing Remotion animations that remain intuitive for coding agents and editable in Remotion Studio Visual Mode. It directs to the canonical Remotion docs pages for interactivity best practices and for making a custom component interactive, and for compositions built mainly from video and audio clips it routes to the video-editing guidance in the companion remotion-markup skill so clips stay editable in the timeline. Use it when structuring Remotion markup, not for scaffolding a project.

items.name: remotion-saas
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Build video SaaS apps with Remotion Player, templates, and client or server rendering choices.
items.summary: Remotion SaaS guides building video applications with Remotion—from simple form-driven renders to full editor experiences. It helps choose templates, embed the Remotion Player for previews, and pick rendering options across Node.js, Lambda, Vercel, and Cloudflare. Use it when shipping a product that generates or previews programmatic video in a web app.

items.name: higgsfield-video-explainer
items.author: higgsfield-ai
items.description: A creator turns a topic or document into a narrated, non-photoreal explainer video assembled from 10-second blocks via the Higgsfield CLI.
items.summary: higgsfield-video-explainer produces a narrated, non-photoreal explainer or story video from a topic or source document using the Higgsfield CLI. The workflow locks one visual style key (from live CMS presets or custom references), writes one narration line and one visual prompt per 10-second block, generates every Seed Audio voice take first and every Gemini Omni clip second, then assembles the ordered pairs server-side with the explainer_video job. It supports mascot or faceless modes, 16:9 or 9:16 aspect, one-to-ten-minute durations, and optional burned subtitles, and it deliberately asks the user for style and production choices in separate turns. Not for photoreal films, ads, talking heads, or editing finished video.

items.name: remotion-docs
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Search and fetch current Remotion API docs while building programmatic video compositions.
items.summary: This skill teaches agents how to discover and read current Remotion documentation instead of relying on memorized API knowledge. It uses the Remotion Algolia search API to find relevant pages, then fetches each page as Markdown by appending .md to the docs URL. The intended workflow is search, select the best hits, pull the Markdown sources, and implement features from up-to-date references. Load Remotion Best Practices when you need authoring guidance rather than raw API lookup.

items.name: animate
items.author: emilkowalski
items.description: Build purposeful UI motion from scratch—deciding whether to animate, which properties, curves, and durations, then writing the code.
items.summary: Animate is a construction skill that turns motion requests into implementations that pass strict design-engineering review. It walks through whether something should animate at all, then selects tools, properties, curves, durations, and exit behavior in the right order. Use it when asked to add transitions, make components feel alive, or build animations from scratch in frontend code.

items.name: gpt-image-2
items.author: prime-skills
items.description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2 on RunComfy for typography, logos, and precise instruction edits.
items.summary: This skill guides agents to generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2 on RunComfy through the runcomfy CLI. It documents GPT Image 2 strengths including embedded text, logos, multilingual typography, and instruction precision, plus its three fixed sizes and edit-with-preservation language. The skill also explains when to route to sibling models like Flux 2 or Nano Banana Pro instead.

items.name: motion-doctrine
items.author: heygen-com
items.description: Gateway motion law for HyperFrames—continuous camera feel, vector seams, and performance-first animation rules.
items.summary: This gateway HyperFrames skill establishes the high-level motion law that makes multi-scene videos feel like one continuous camera move. It defines the vector law, film current, carrier elements, causal motion, Seam Gate enforcement, and rules against idle wobble between beats. Authoring order starts with a vector ledger, seam stamping, sustained-motion routes, then verification via seam-gate scripts. Load it first before any HyperFrames animation; it routes to cut-the-curve, oversized-cursor, and seam-craft for implementation.

items.name: captions-overlay
items.author: heygen-com
items.description: Apply HyperFrames caption overlay doctrine for talking-head and launch videos without reserved keep-out bands.
items.summary: This HyperFrames skill defines caption overlay doctrine for talking-head and product launch videos. Captions are composited on top of the film using drop, rail, or embed models rather than reserving a bottom keep-out band that shifts content upward. It applies on top of the embedded-captions upstream skill and quotes the rail-plus-embed model from product-launch-video scene guidance. Load it when adding subtitles or deciding how phrases should ride the rail versus embed at climax moments.

items.name: cut-the-curve
items.author: heygen-com
items.description: Implement HyperFrames velocity-matched seams, waterfall entries, and nudge curves for transitions and kinetic text.
items.summary: This HyperFrames technique catalog documents five velocity-matched seam transitions plus two in-scene techniques. Seams include zoom-through, inverse zoom-through, cut-the-curve, waterfall cut, and rack-focus blur-cut with mirrored power4 eases and partial-travel matching. In-scene techniques cover waterfall entry for title cards and the nudge curve for slow-fast-slow group repositioning. Read it before authoring any transition, text-beat handoff, kinetic text entry, or group slide in HyperFrames films.

items.name: seam-craft
items.author: heygen-com
items.description: Fix HyperFrames master-timeline seam render issues like white flashes and opacity dips at scene cuts.
items.summary: This HyperFrames skill covers render-correctness prerequisites for scene-to-scene seams on the master timeline. It explains the opaque stage-ground white-flash guard, how overlapping scene wrappers blend, final-frame holds, track ping-pong behavior, and lint-clean template stamping. Load it when assembling index.html, debugging white flashes at cuts, or verifying opacity dips on dark films. It does not replace the transition registry—that remains in cut-the-curve.

items.name: changelog-video
items.author: heygen-com
items.description: Turn a weekly changelog markdown into a branded square changelog video with VO, mock UI, and captions.
items.summary: This self-contained HyperFrames skill turns a weekly changelog markdown digest into a finished branded changelog video. Output is a square 1080 film around 45-60 seconds with Annie voiceover, animated brand background, mock-UI visualizations, and lowkey captions. It mandates loading motion-doctrine, cut-the-curve, seam-craft, and captions-overlay before authoring. The pipeline writes a lint-clean project under projects/active/weekly-changelog-<range>/ and renders only when explicitly requested.

items.name: oversized-cursor
items.author: heygen-com
items.description: Animate house-style oversized macOS cursors that carry the eye and click-ignite the next beat in UI scenes.
items.summary: This HyperFrames skill defines the house-style oversized macOS cursor technique for launch and UI demo videos. The cursor enters from off-screen, tip-targets interactive elements, performs a click that ignites the next beat, and exits with cross-scene handoff rules. Brand-motif cursor variants are supported. Load it whenever a scene involves pointers, UI kickoffs, morph or typing ignition, or when static frames need motion to carry the viewer's eye.

items.name: remotion-upgrade
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Upgrade Remotion, @remotion packages, Mediabunny deps, and installed Remotion agent skills safely across workspaces.
items.summary: Upgrade Remotion projects by detecting the package manager, running npx remotion upgrade when available, or manually aligning all remotion and @remotion/* dependencies to the latest stable version. Also updates compatible Mediabunny packages and installed Remotion agent skills. Use when asked to upgrade, update, or bump a Remotion codebase.

items.name: archify
items.author: tt-a1i
items.description: Generate polished architecture, workflow, sequence, and state diagrams as standalone HTML with export.
items.summary: Creates professional architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle diagrams as standalone HTML files with inline SVG, dark and light themes, and one-click export to PNG, JPEG, WebP, or SVG. It accepts plain-language descriptions or pasted Mermaid code and can inspect repository evidence when diagrams must reflect real systems. Use when users need system architecture visuals, runbooks, CI flows, or beautified Mermaid diagrams.

items.name: review-loop
items.author: 2dmurali
items.description: Run an iterative worker-reviewer loop that scores output 1-10 and revises until a quality gate is met.
items.summary: Review Loop implements an iterative worker-reviewer cycle inside a single agent session: complete the task, spawn a critic to score it 1-10 with specific feedback, revise, and repeat until the quality gate is met. Defaults require at least two loops and stop at four or when the score reaches 8/10. Use it for implementations, specs, or reviews where quality matters more than speed and clear acceptance criteria exist.

items.name: remotion-maps
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Animate maps in Remotion videos using Mapbox, MapLibre, MapTiler, static images, or CesiumJS techniques.
items.summary: Remotion Maps is a skill for animating geographic visuals inside Remotion compositions. It routes each shot to one self-contained technique—static satellite images, Mapbox, free MapLibre, MapTiler annotations, or CesiumJS terrain flythroughs—each with its own TECHNIQUE.md guide. Use it when a programmatic video needs map zooms, globe views, labeled regions, or flight-simulator-style camera moves.

items.name: remotion-multimedia
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Read audio and video metadata and durations in Remotion using the Mediabunny browser multimedia library.
items.summary: Remotion Multimedia teaches agents to work with Mediabunny—the browser multimedia library for audio and video inside Remotion projects. It covers extracting audio duration, video dimensions, and video duration through focused task guides rather than one monolithic API tour. Use it when a Remotion composition must measure media files accurately before sequencing clips, captions, or transitions.

items.name: ask-sonner
items.author: emilkowalski
items.description: Implement Sonner React toast notifications with theming promise and positioning patterns.
items.summary: Guide to Sonner React toast library covering Toaster setup, toast() variants, promise and loading toasts, updating, dismissing, styling, theming, icons, positioning, and troubleshooting missing styles or duplicate toasts with Tailwind.

items.name: browser-mcp-agent
items.author: antibrow
items.description: Give agents a real fingerprinted browser over MCP—navigate, click, fill, screenshot—with persistent logged-in profiles.
items.summary: Browser MCP Agent runs antibrow as an MCP server so AI agents control a real, fingerprinted browser through tool calls without Playwright code. Sessions persist across runs with coherent device fingerprints that avoid headless detection. Use it when agents must operate logged-in sites, need computer-use browsing, or compare hosted browser services for autonomous web tasks.

items.name: multi-account-isolation
items.author: antibrow
items.description: Verify anti-detect browser profiles are truly isolated across timezone, WebRTC, canvas hashes, and cookie jars before running multi-account QA.
items.summary: Multi-account-isolation is a verification skill for anti-detect browser profiles used in authorized QA and multi-identity testing. It walks through concrete checks—timezone vs exit IP, WebRTC leaks, canvas and WebGL hash stability, persona uniqueness, cookie jar separation, and fleet-wide address collisions—rather than assuming vendor claims. The workflow includes SDK setup examples, ranked failure diagnosis, and guidance on what runtime artifacts stay local versus what leaves the machine. Use it when several owned accounts run from one machine and you need evidence the browser layer is internally consistent before scaling automation.

items.name: agent-pulse
items.author: Jane-o-O-o-O
items.description: Inspect local AI agent sessions, token usage, tool calls, costs, and health across Claude, Cursor, Codex, and other agent logs.
items.summary: Operate the agent-pulse CLI to inspect local AI agent activity across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Aider, and other tool logs. Summarize sessions, token usage, tool and search calls, model mix, estimated costs, budgets, forecasts, and health reports. Use when auditing agent spend or diagnosing setup issues rather than reading source code manually.

items.name: landing-page-conversion-audit
items.author: autonnel
items.description: Audit landing, sales, or checkout pages for conversion leaks and return a ranked fix list by expected revenue impact.
items.summary: Landing-page-conversion-audit reviews live landing, sales, opt-in, product, or checkout pages for conversion leaks on paid traffic. It gathers available traffic, funnel, and device data, then evaluates message match, mobile above-the-fold clarity, offer transparency, form friction, trust at payment, post-purchase paths, and tracking health. Findings must name the element, failure mode, and specific change with effort and confidence—not vague CRO platitudes. Use when conversion rate is low or before scaling ads; skip when there is no traffic or the offer itself is broken.

items.name: sales-funnel-blueprint
items.author: autonnel
items.description: Turn an offer into a build-ready multi-step funnel spec with pages, price ladder, metrics, and instrumentation blockers.
items.summary: Sales-funnel-blueprint converts an offer into an implementable multi-step funnel specification. It forces five inputs—offer and price, traffic source, awareness level, fulfillment model, and existing assets—then selects a standard funnel shape and produces page-by-page specs with headlines, proof, objections, fields, pricing, exit paths, and success metrics. It also defines the price ladder, instrumentation blockers, and build order. The output is handoff-ready for builders or agents. Use before writing copy or picking tools; not for auditing an existing underperforming page.

items.name: server-side-conversion-tracking
items.author: autonnel
items.description: Implement server-side conversion tracking with click-id capture, order attachment, CAPI postbacks, and dedupe for Meta, TikTok, Google, and Bing.
items.summary: Server-side-conversion-tracking explains how to report purchases accurately to Facebook, TikTok, Google, and Bing using Conversions API and offline import patterns. Browser pixels lose conversions to iOS restrictions, ad blockers, and cross-domain cookie loss; this skill walks the required order—capture click ids on first landing hit, persist server-side, carry across funnel steps, attach to orders, send queued server events with dedupe ids, and verify against your database. It also states what server-side tracking cannot fix, such as cross-platform attribution disagreements. Use when platform-reported sales diverge from real orders or when launching new paid funnels.

items.name: browser-fingerprint-audit
items.author: liarjsdev
items.description: Run a liarjs CLI audit that scores canvas, WebGL, audio, fonts, and network fingerprint consistency.
items.summary: Walks agents through auditing a browser fingerprint for internal contradictions with the liarjs CLI. It probes canvas, WebGL, WebGL2, WebGPU, audio, fonts, WebRTC, and timezone signals, then scores them against the TLS, HTTP, and ASN view of the same request. Use when running fingerprint tests, checking canvas or WebGL stability, or determining whether a browser profile is self-consistent.

items.name: funnel-platform-picker
items.author: autonnel
items.description: Choose a funnel or landing page platform by modeling true total cost, lock-in, and operational fit—not feature checklists.
items.summary: Funnel-platform-picker helps choose landing and funnel software by computing real total cost, data ownership, and lock-in for a specific case. It gathers six inputs—monthly funnel GMV, funnel count, contact list size, catalog location, maintenance capacity, and exit tolerance—then models hosted flat-fee, percentage-of-revenue, WordPress plugin, Shopify app, and self-hosted cost curves including migration labour. Recommendations must state the downside of each path and verify open-source licence claims rather than trusting marketing. Use when evaluating ClickFunnels alternatives, cutting funnel SaaS costs, or deciding whether self-hosting is worth operational overhead.

items.name: playwright-stealth-verify
items.author: liarjsdev
items.description: Assert Playwright or Puppeteer pages present a coherent browser fingerprint via liarjs library checks.
items.summary: Shows how to verify whether an automated browser looks coherent using liarjs against a Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or CDP Page you already control. It checks navigator.webdriver, HeadlessChrome tokens, worker versus main-thread identity, patched-API integrity, and WebGL versus WebGPU GPU identity. Use when stealth plugin effects need measuring or fingerprint quality assertions belong in a test suite.

items.name: fingerprint-ci-gate
items.author: liarjsdev
items.description: Fail CI when browser fingerprint consistency regresses against a saved liarjs baseline scan.
items.summary: Teaches agents to gate builds on browser fingerprint regressions using liarjs. Save a baseline scan as JSON, compare later runs in CI, and fail the job when the consistency score falls below a threshold. Use when adding fingerprint or headless-detection checks to GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or other pipelines to catch Chromium or scraping harness regressions before they ship.

items.name: post-purchase-upsell-flow
items.author: autonnel
items.description: Design one-click post-purchase upsells and downsells that raise AOV without risking the main checkout conversion rate.
items.summary: Post-purchase-upsell-flow designs one-click upsell and downsell steps that increase average order value after payment is captured. It explains why post-purchase offers are safer than checkout bumps, how to craft complementary single-decision screens, and the technical requirements for vaulted payment methods, merged orders, deferred ERP pushes, per-charge refunds, and updated purchase values for ad optimization. Includes provider notes for Stripe, PayPal, and SCA fallbacks plus metrics like take rate, AOV lift, and refund guardrails. Use when thank-you pages are dead-ends or AOV is too low for the same ad spend—not when the main funnel barely converts.

items.name: self-hosted-funnel-launch
items.author: autonnel
items.description: Deploy and publish a self-hosted sales funnel with checkout, upsells, and agent-driven MCP control.
items.summary: Guides agents through deploying Autonnel as a self-hosted ClickFunnels alternative, from empty install to a published funnel with landing page, checkout, one-click upsell, and thank-you flow. Covers Cloudflare Workers and Docker paths, Postgres setup, payment wiring, and the MCP surface that lets agents create and edit funnels programmatically. Use when asked to build, host, or operate a sales funnel on your own infrastructure cheaply.

items.name: fingerprint-failure-triage
items.author: liarjsdev
items.description: Attribute each failing liarjs check id to launch config, stealth layer, network path, or machine image.
items.summary: Helps agents read a liarjs fingerprint report and attribute each failing check to the component that produced it. It explains what check ids such as webdriver, worker-consistency, gpu-triad, native-integrity, and tz measure, and whether the signal comes from launch configuration, page-modifying layers, the network path, or the machine image. Use when a scan returns a low score and you need an owner list instead of just a number.

items.name: herdr
items.author: herdrdev
items.description: Control Herdr terminal multiplexer panes, tabs, workspaces, and coding agents from inside a Herdr session.
items.summary: Herdr is a terminal multiplexer skill that lets coding agents inspect and control their Herdr session—workspaces, tabs, panes, shells, and neighboring agents—through the herdr CLI. It only activates when the user explicitly mentions Herdr and the agent is running inside a Herdr-managed pane with HERDR_ENV set. Use it to read pane output, start agents, manage layout, or coordinate parallel terminal work without guessing CLI syntax.

items.name: higgsfield-brandkit
items.author: higgsfield-ai
items.description: Build and extend full visual brand systems—palettes, SVG logos, typography, mockups, packaging, and brandbooks via Higgsfield CLI plus local tooling.
items.summary: Higgsfield-brandkit creates and extends complete visual brand systems through the Higgsfield CLI and bundled local scripts. It supports palettes, SVG logo marks, typography, mockups, social graphics, packaging, signage, merchandise, posters, decks, and editable brandbooks while preserving supplied official assets. A Brand Lock records constraints, approvals persist in local state, and downstream outputs regenerate only when foundation slots change. Use for new identities or applying existing branding across deliverables—not for general unbranded image generation or website implementation.

items.name: higgsfield-youtube-thumbnail
items.author: higgsfield-ai
items.description: Generate high-CTR YouTube thumbnails and vertical video covers with identity-locked faces, logos, and surgical Seedream edits via Higgsfield CLI.
items.summary: Higgsfield-youtube-thumbnail creates click-worthy YouTube thumbnails and vertical covers through the Higgsfield CLI. It enforces truthful concepts, preserves up to three referenced identities, supports logos and controlled variants, renders with Nano Banana Pro, and applies focused Seedream edits for expression or background tweaks. The workflow covers intake gates, concept frameworks, prompt contracts, post-render vision QA, and optional headline overlays. Chain it after a video workflow when the topic is known; it is not for generating the video itself or product catalog shots.

items.name: remotion-studio
items.author: remotion-dev
items.description: Launch Remotion Studio to preview programmatic video compositions in the browser.
items.summary: Instructs agents to preview Remotion video projects by running npx remotion studio --no-open and opening the printed URL in a browser. If Studio is already running, the command prints the existing URL and exits; otherwise it starts the long-running preview server. Use when a Remotion composition needs interactive timeline preview during development.

items.name: caveman-explore
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Discover and install Caveman skills from the ecosystem catalog.
items.summary: caveman-explore helps users discover Caveman skills available for their workflow and install the ones that fit. It is part of the Caveman skill suite focused on finding capabilities before execution. Use it when exploring what Caveman offers or choosing skills for a new project.

items.name: caveman-optimize
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Enable Caveman gateway optimization to reduce LLM cost after measurement baseline exists.
items.summary: caveman-optimize enables LLM cost optimization through the Caveman gateway after measurement is in place. It assumes record-mode observability is already configured and walks through turning on optimizers with proper eval gates. Use it when users want to reduce LLM spend based on verified usage data.

items.name: caveman-learn
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Capture durable lessons from agent sessions into reusable Caveman skill knowledge.
items.summary: caveman-learn captures durable knowledge from agent sessions into the Caveman skill system. It distills decisions, rationales, and reusable patterns worth preserving across conversations. Use it after sessions that produced insights that should inform future agent behavior.

items.name: safe-refactor
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Refactor code safely with tests, incremental steps, and rollback awareness.
items.summary: safe-refactor is a Caveman skill for structural code improvements that preserve behavior. It emphasizes incremental steps, test coverage or equivalent verification, and avoiding risky big-bang rewrites. Use it when refactoring modules, APIs, or backend logic where regressions would be costly.

items.name: investigate-first
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Diagnose ambiguous bugs and performance regressions with evidence before changing code.
items.summary: Investigate-first is a Caveman debugging skill that makes agents gather proof before touching product code. It applies to intermittent failures, unknown root causes, and performance regressions where guessing leads to churn. The workflow ranks hypotheses, traces state transitions, and stops when one mechanism explains the evidence.

items.name: verify-and-stop
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Prove work meets acceptance criteria with focused checks then stop without scope creep.
items.summary: verify-and-stop is a Caveman skill for validation-only tasks that prove acceptance without expanding scope. It translates criteria into focused checks, distinguishes pass from blocked, and stops when proof is complete. Agents must not edit product code or add unrelated tests unless fixes are explicitly requested.

items.name: surgical-patch
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Apply the smallest correct code change to fix a known issue without drive-by edits.
items.summary: surgical-patch guides agents to make the smallest correct change that fixes a known issue. It rejects drive-by refactors, formatting sweeps, and unrelated edits. Use it when the fix scope is clear and the goal is a focused patch rather than broader improvement work.

items.name: caveman-evidence-review
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Review code or claims with evidence discipline before approving changes.
items.summary: caveman-evidence-review applies evidence discipline when reviewing code, plans, or agent outputs. It requires claims to be backed by observable proof and rejects unsupported assertions. Use it during review gates where quality depends on verified facts rather than confident narration.

items.name: caveman-discover
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Find relevant Caveman skills and workflows for a stated problem or task.
items.summary: caveman-discover helps users find Caveman skills and workflows suited to their current task. It matches stated problems to catalog capabilities before agents execute work. Use it at the start of a session when unsure which Caveman skill fits the request.

items.name: lean-build
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Ship the smallest useful increment with tight scope and no speculative extras.
items.summary: lean-build is a Caveman skill that keeps agent implementation tightly scoped to the smallest useful increment. It rejects speculative features, premature abstractions, and drive-by improvements. Use it when building features where speed and focus matter more than exhaustive polish.

items.name: caveman-manage
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Manage installed Caveman skills including updates, removal, and configuration.
items.summary: caveman-manage handles ongoing administration of installed Caveman skills. It supports updating, removing, and configuring skills in the Caveman ecosystem after initial setup. Use it when maintaining the skill collection rather than discovering or installing for the first time.

items.name: migration
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Execute reversible schema, data, API, or config migrations with rollback proof.
items.summary: migration is a Caveman skill for implementing compatibility-safe transitions across schema, data, APIs, protocols, configuration, or dependencies. It maps readers, writers, and ownership, defines rollback paths, and sequences expand-migrate-verify-contract steps. Agents stop after the requested stage passes without implicit destructive contraction.

items.name: caveman-setup
items.author: JuliusBrussee
items.description: Wire a repository through the Caveman gateway for LLM cost and latency measurement.
items.summary: caveman-setup wires a repository through the Caveman Cloud gateway so every LLM request is measured for cost, tokens, and latency. It performs minimal verified integration in record mode only, keeping secrets in env vars and reporting only observed verification results. Optimization and savings claims are explicitly out of scope.

items.name: flutter-apply-architecture-best-practices
items.author: flutter
items.description: Architect Flutter apps with layered UI, logic, and data separation using MVVM and scalable project structure.
items.summary: Architect Flutter applications using a recommended layered approach separating UI, logic, and data with strict separation of concerns. Implements MVVM in the presentation layer with lean widgets, view models for state, and repositories for data access. Use when structuring a new Flutter project or refactoring for scalability and maintainability.

items.name: self-improving-agent
items.author: zhaono1
items.description: Continuously improve agent skills and codebase from session outcomes using multi-memory learning and hook-driven self-correction.
items.summary: A universal self-improving agent skill that learns from every skill run using semantic, episodic, and working memory. It auto-triggers on skill completion or errors via hooks, self-corrects, and can evolve the codebase over time. Use when building agents that should continuously improve workflows and skill libraries from real session outcomes.

items.name: flutter-build-responsive-layout
items.author: flutter

items.summary: find-the-original-image is an OSINT skill for reverse image search across Yandex, Google Lens, Bing Visual Search, TinEye, and Baidu. Its goal is provenance: finding the earliest publication of an image and reading that page for the photographer, date, caption, and names. It provides an engine-selection table keyed to the input (faces to Yandex, products and in-image text to Google Lens, region search to Bing, oldest-copy sorting to TinEye, Chinese content to Baidu), recommends running at least three engines, and teaches the crop-and-retry technique that finds matches full-frame search misses. This skill is investigative tooling and does not fit the builder-journey taxonomy cleanly.

items.name: investigate-without-getting-made
items.author: UseOSINT
items.description: Investigators and researchers use it to run online investigations without alerting the subject: threat-modeling observers, controlling IP and browser fingerprints, and building sockpuppet personas.
items.summary: An investigator OPSEC skill for conducting open-source investigations without tipping off the subject. It starts from a threat model - who might notice the collection, what they would see, and what the consequence would be - and prescribes a proportionate posture, from a normal browser for public registries up to compartmented hardware for high-risk targets. It details the attribution surface a visit exposes (IP and ASN, browser and TLS fingerprints, locale, timing patterns, logged-in accounts), covers building and aging sockpuppet research personas with burner verification, and weighs VPN versus residential proxy versus Tor. Its core warning: most investigators are burned by platform features like profile-view notifications, not by IP leaks.

items.name: is-this-photo-real
items.author: UseOSINT
items.description: An investigator or fact-checker uses it to test whether an image or video is authentic, original, and correctly captioned, from provenance search down to pixel forensics.
items.summary: is-this-photo-real is an OSINT verification workflow for testing whether an image or video is authentic, original, and correctly captioned. Its ordering is the method: provenance first, pixels last - chase the earliest upload and its caption before touching forensic filters, because most deceptive media is real footage with a false caption. The workflow proceeds through metadata and C2PA Content Credentials, internal consistency (signage, plates, weather, season against the claimed date and place), physical consistency (lighting, shadows, perspective), and only then signal-level forensics like noise residuals and double-compression analysis. It also documents the failure modes of AI-detector tools and warns against running error level analysis on platform-processed files. Use it for fact-checking media, deepfake assessment, or disinformation cases.

It teaches which record fields matter — service membership, registration dates, usernames, and signup IPs beat the credentials themselves — and how to choose a source for each question. It draws a firm ethical line: leaked passwords are linkage evidence for analysis, never inputs to a login form. Use it for self-audits, client remediation, or OSINT investigation of an identity's breach footprint.
